images.caption: Figure 1:Mitigating Explanation Drift via Semantic Anchoring.Saliency maps for “Electric Guitar” sample after continual learning. Standard CL (PLAN) suffers from explanation drift, shifting attention to spurious background artifacts. While pixel-level methods (RRR) attempt to mitigate this, they result in noisy, non-specific attributions. OurC3Lanchors model representations to semantically meaningful concepts, maintaining focus on diagnostic features like the fretboard and guitar body.

Figure 2:C3LOverview.Discriminative visual concepts are discovered offline via an LLM and spatially
grounded using SAM 3, producing model-state-independent supervision targets that
break the self-referential drift loop of prior pixel-level methods. During continual
training,ℒconcept\mathcal{L}_{\text{concept}}anchors relevance to semantic regions via
acrowding-out effect, whileℒstab\mathcal{L}_{\text{stab}}preserves
background spatial structure against task-specific drift.
